stem: A child with chronic neutropaenia is otherwise well, but the family asks what serious infective complication may still occur; which is the best answer?
explanation: Sepsis is the serious infective complication that may still occur in chronic neutropaenia. Even when a child is otherwise asymptomatic, chronic neutropaenia can be associated with bacterial infection and sepsis.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because sepsis is specifically recognised as a possible serious infective complication in chronic neutropaenia.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because appendicitis is not a typical complication of chronic neutropaenia.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because croup is not the serious infective complication described here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because migraine is unrelated to chronic neutropaenia and infection risk.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because constipation is not an infective complication of chronic neutropaenia.
